The UK Ministry of Defence tightens scrutiny of military aircraft supply chains, pressuring tech stocks

The UK military has tightened its review of supply chains for Chinese tech companies after military drones were detected by China. As a result, tech stocks face regulatory risks.

The UK Ministry of Defence recently found that some military drones used components from Chinese companies, and as a result, the drones were detected by China at their locations. This incident made the UK military realize that technology from Chinese companies may pose security risks and threaten national security. Therefore, the UK Ministry of Defence has decided that, going forward, when procuring military equipment, it will more strictly review whether those devices contain parts from Chinese companies. This decision will affect all companies doing business with Chinese tech companies, such as chip manufacturers, software suppliers, and others. These companies may face more scrutiny and fewer orders.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Due to this decision by the UK Ministry of Defence, the market may become concerned about stocks linked to Chinese tech companies, causing their prices to fall. Capital may flow out of these stocks and into those viewed as safer.
- Medium term: This decision may accelerate global attention to supply-chain security, leading more countries to increase scrutiny of products from Chinese tech companies. This could reshape global supply chains: some Chinese tech firms may lose some international market share, while companies without Chinese business may gain new opportunities.

My take
I believe this is a neutral-to-negative development, mainly affecting companies that do business with Chinese tech firms. In the short term, these companies’ share prices may come under pressure. But in the long run, it could drive supply-chain diversification worldwide, reducing reliance on a single country—something that could be good for the global technology sector. I suggest that investors focus on companies with a high level of supply-chain diversification, as they may be better able to cope with future regulatory changes.

translatedData.content: Little knowledge｜What is the funding rate? It’s open-ended contracts—don’t let it steal your profits. Perpetual contracts settle the funding rate every 8 hours: a positive rate means longs are paying shorts (the longs pay the shorts); a negative rate means shorts pay longs. When the market is euphoric and the funding rate spikes to an outrageous positive value, it often signals that longs are crowded and the risk of a pullback is building. Before trading contracts, develop the habit of checking the funding rate—it can help you avoid many traps like “buying the hype and getting liquidated.” The funding rate does not include trading fees; it’s pure financing cost. title: ETH at $1,881: The Bounce That Lost Its Grip
subTitle:
Ethereum looks strangely quiet at $1,881.07.

But the 15-minute chart tells a less comfortable story.

ETH climbed from the $1,876.10 area and eventually printed $1,886.59. For a while, the candles kept making higher pushes.

Then the character changed.

A sharp red candle cut through the short-term averages, and ETH slipped back toward $1,880.

That move matters more to me than the tiny -0.05% shown beside the price.

The first thing I notice is the moving-average arrangement.

The 7-MA sits at $1,883.05.

The 25-MA is almost identical at $1,883.61.

ETH is below both.

The 99-MA, however, is down around $1,878.95.

So the short-term picture has weakened, but price hasn't completely broken the deeper structure visible on this chart.

That creates an interesting little battlefield between roughly $1,879 and $1,884.

Above it, buyers have something to reclaim.

Below it, the earlier low around $1,876.10 becomes much harder to ignore.

The quiet detail is the way ETH reacted after reaching $1,886.59.

It didn't simply fall once.

It tried to recover.

Then sellers appeared again.

That second failure is often more informative than the first red candle. It suggests the market wasn't merely reacting to one burst of selling; higher prices were having difficulty attracting enough follow-through.

And volume adds another layer.

The chart shows elevated activity around the larger candles, while the latest bars remain relatively modest compared with some earlier bursts.

That's why I wouldn't read this as a simple "ETH is bearish" chart.

It looks more like momentum has been interrupted.

There is a difference.

Ethereum's fundamentals are also moving in a direction that the 15-minute chart cannot capture.

The Ethereum roadmap lists Glamsterdam as an upcoming H2 2026 upgrade, with work focused on scaling how Ethereum processes transactions and manages its growing database.

The Ethereum Foundation's 2026 protocol priorities also emphasize three broad areas: scaling, improving user experience, and hardening the L1's security and resilience.

That's the part I find easy to forget when staring at five-minute or fifteen-minute candles.

A red candle doesn't erase years of protocol development.

But protocol development doesn't automatically rescue a weak short-term chart either.

Both things can be true.

And right now, the screenshot captures that tension nicely.

ETH is around $1,881.

The 7-MA and 25-MA are clustered around $1,883–$1,884.

The 99-MA sits near $1,879.

The recent high is $1,886.59.

The visible low is $1,876.10.

Those aren't predictions.

They're simply the places where the market has already shown its hand.

Recent market reporting has also placed ETH below $1,900 amid broader crypto weakness, suggesting this small 15-minute struggle is happening inside a larger market that hasn't found convincing momentum yet.

And that makes the current chart more interesting.

Because ETH doesn't need a spectacular candle to reveal something.

If price can reclaim the short-term averages and stay there, the recent sell-off starts looking more like a temporary interruption.

If it keeps getting rejected underneath them, the $1,879 area becomes increasingly important.

And if that deeper level gives way, traders watching this particular structure will naturally look back toward the $1,876.10 low.

No prediction required.

Just observation.

Ethereum has spent years becoming infrastructure while the market keeps trying to reduce it to a blinking number on a screen.

This screenshot is a good reminder that both versions exist at once.

The network keeps building in the background.

The chart keeps arguing about a few dollars.

Sometimes the most revealing moment is when those two timelines barely seem connected.

translatedData.content:
In the robotics industry, it’s possible to sell even just the “shell” and still achieve a huge market valuation.

But from an engineering perspective, the truly difficult part may not be mechanical capability.

Motors, joints, reducers, sensors, mechanical structures—although these have technical barriers, at their core they are all relatively well-defined engineering problems. As the supply chain matures, production scales up, and technologies iterate, mechanical capability will eventually converge.

What’s truly hard is model capability, as well as safety capability and privacy protection.

Once robots enter the real world, it’s not just about whether they can move. It’s whether they can understand the environment, judge situations, plan actions, handle exceptions, and remain stable in complex scenarios.

Mechanical capability is like a fixed target, while model capability is a moving target.

So in the long run, a robot’s real core competitiveness probably isn’t about whose robot looks more human, has more joints, or moves more smoothly. It’s about who has a stronger model, richer real-world data, and a more reliable safety system.

Mechanics is the body; the model is the brain. What will truly be valuable in the future robotics industry may not be that “shell,” but the intelligence hidden behind it.

Otherwise, you just end up with a giant toy. Betting on Tesla—its visual capabilities, privacy and security, and models already show a certain level of strength.

To the robots in China—come on, young ones.

Not long ago, when you were obedient and entered the humanoid robotics industry, selling shells and selling concepts could still “circle money” in the capital markets.

Now, a company comes out that talks about model capability, privacy and security, and visual spatial perception—and it can also “circle money.” Are there brothers in related fields? Or it’s still possible to创业圈米—there’s just too much capital already accumulated in financial markets, especially in China. If you “circle” for long enough, you become a giant.

In the past, many mechanical patents were public patents, and there were fewer challenging targets that needed serious effort in mechanical engineering.

Mars Finance news: On August 15, Unitree Technology’s IPO on the STAR Market has drawn intense market attention. The initial public offering price is 150.80 yuan per share. The company is expected to raise about 6.099 billion yuan, and its total market capitalization after the offering is approximately 60.993 billion yuan. As a member of “Hangzhou’s Six Little Dragons,” Unitree Technology is viewed by the market as A-share’s “No. 1 listed company in humanoid robots.” The company submitted its IPO application in March 2026, and successfully passed the review in June—taking only 73 days—setting the fastest approval record since the implementation of the STAR Market pre-review mechanism. 

In the secondary market, Unitree Technology has become one of the hottest new-share subscription targets this year. On average, only 1 person out of about 5,500 investors secured a winning bid. Based on the first-day price increase, a single winning bid (500 shares) could yield a potential profit of about 200,000 to 300,000 yuan. 

For this IPO, the strategic allocation lineup is well-stacked, including the National Social Security Fund, DeepSeek, CNPC Kunlun Capital, Southern Power Grid Industrial Finance Holding, Tianyi Capital, Tencent-affiliated investment institutions, and CICC Investment, among others. Institutions such as Meituan, Sequoia China, GROWTH Capital, Shunwei Capital, Tencent, Alibaba, Ant Group, and others also hold shares in the company. 

Industry insiders believe that Unitree Technology’s listing will provide the first secondary-market valuation anchor for the embodied-intelligence robot sector, helping capital shift its focus from technical-concept speculation to validation of commercialization capabilities. It is expected that more robot companies will enter the capital markets in the future.

content:
机器人行业，光是卖“壳子”都能卖出很大的市值。

但从工程角度看，真正困难的可能并不是机械能力。

电机、关节、减速器、传感器、机械结构，这些东西虽然有技术门槛，但本质上都是相对明确的工程问题。随着供应链成熟、规模化生产和技术迭代，机械能力终究会逐渐趋同。

真正难的是模型能力，以及安全能力和隐私保护。

机器人进入现实世界以后，不只是“能不能动”，而是能不能理解环境、判断情况、规划动作、处理异常，并在复杂场景下保持稳定。

机械能力更像是一个固定靶，而模型能力是一个不断移动的靶。

所以长期来看，机器人真正的核心竞争力，可能并不是谁的机器人长得更像人、关节更多、动作更丝滑，而是谁拥有更强的模型、更丰富的现实世界数据，以及更可靠的安全体系。

机械是躯体，模型才是大脑。未来机器人产业真正值钱的，可能不是那个“壳子”，而是藏在壳子背后的智能。

不然就走向了一个大玩具，押注特斯拉，他在视觉、隐私安全、以及模型上都有一定的能力。

国内机器人，加油吧、少年。

不过多年前听话，跻身进入人形机器人行业，卖壳子、卖概念、都能在资本市场圈米。

现在出来一家谈模型能力、隐私安全、视觉空间感知的机器人公司，也能圈米。有相关从业的兄弟？还是可以创业圈米，金融市场沉淀的资金还是太多，尤其国内，狠狠的圈，圈的时间够久，就成巨头。

过去很多机械专利都是公开的专利，机械上需要努力的目标比较少。

title: LDO 观察：守着 180 亿金库，却拿着 0.3 刀的治理票根
subTitle:
我把 SSV 拆了一遍，后台不少朋友让我顺手看看 LDO。说实话，写之前我犹豫了一下——Lido 太熟了，熟到容易写成白皮书复读机。但翻完 2026 年上半年的数据，我发现这项目现在的拧巴程度，其实比 SSV 更有意思。

一句话先给结论：Lido 协议是以太坊质押的最大玩家，年入几千万美金；但 LDO 这个币从高点跌了 96%，现在只有 0.3 刀左右。协议赚钱，代币不沾光，这情况在加密圈不算新鲜，但 Lido 做得特别极致。

先看基本面：stETH 已经是金融基础设施

2020 年 12 月上线的东西，没必要再复述白皮书了。直接看 2026 年 8 月现在的实况：

Lido 守着 945 万枚 ETH，约 180 亿美金 TVL。虽然市场占有率从巅峰的 32% 回落到现在的 21%-23%，被 BlackRock、BitMine 这些机构托管和 ether.fi 之类的 LRT 分流了一些增量，但 stETH 在 Aave、Curve、Maker 里的抵押深度，至今没有任何一个 LST 能撼动。

它的节点运营商分三档：35 家 Curated 机构（占了 89% 的份额）、Obol/SSV 的 DVT 集群、还有 600 多家社区质押节点。最近在推 CMv2，要把原来的 32 ETH 小验证者打包成 2048 ETH 的大节点，验证者总数从 88 万砍到 62.8 万。这对以太坊网络是减负，但对"Lido 中心化"的批评是个缓和剂。

核心矛盾：收着租，但没给代币安插座

这是我看完数据最想吐槽的地方。

以太坊质押的收益链条很清楚：用户存 ETH，拿 90% 的出块奖励，剩下 10% 归 Lido。这 10% 里，5% 给节点运营商当辛苦费，5% 进 Lido DAO 财库。

2025 年 DAO 财库进账 3700-4000 万美金，2026 年年化跑到了 7100 万美金。这笔钱躺在财库里（2026 年 4 月约 1.21 亿美金），由 LDO 持有者投票决定怎么花。

问题是，LDO 持有人自己拿不到这一分钱。

这五年里，LDO 的功能只有一样：投票。没有分红，没有 fee switch，没有质押生息。财库里的钱再多，和你手里的 LDO 也没关系。这就导致了一个极其诡异的现象：协议赚麻了，币价跌麻了。

2026 年唯一的变量是"买回"（Buyback）。有个叫 NEST 的机制，条件是 ETH 价格大于 3000 且年收入大于 4000 万美金，每年最多买 1000 万美金的 LDO。但截至 8 月，这两个条件没同时满足过，所以一分钱都没花出去。之前 3 月份搞过一次 2000 万美金的单笔回购，那属于一次性行为，不是持续的现金流。

监管与筹码：比你想的安全，也比你想的无聊

很多人担心 LDO 被 SEC 盯上。2026 年 3 月的监管指引其实给了定心丸：ETH 被认定为数字商品，stETH 这种液态质押收据没被划为证券。所以 LDO 在合规层面的压力不算大。

真正的隐患是另一个：Lido 控制了全网 21%-28% 的验证者。以太坊社区内部一直有个不成文的红线——"别超过 1/3"。虽然现在没出事，但这始终是悬在头顶的一把刀。

再看筹码结构：

总量 10 亿枚，无通胀，流通 8.49 亿；

团队和投资人解锁早在 2023 年就结束了，剩下的抛压主要来自财库的运营支出；

治理投票率常年只有 5%-6%。

这说明什么？说明大部分人买 LDO 要么是忘了，要么是在赌"哪天 fee switch 开了能分钱"。但目前来看，这种意愿非常低。

2026 下半年盯什么？

如果你手里拿着 LDO，或者打算建仓，接下来这几个节点比 K 线重要：

NEST 能不能真买到币：别看提案写得漂亮，只要 ETH 不站稳 3000，或者收入波动一下，买回计划就是张废纸。

CMv2 的落地：把 32 ETH 验证者合并成大节点，看会不会引发新的中心化争议，或者影响以太坊的多样性。

Dual Governance 的压力测试：stETH 持有人对 LDO 治理有否决权，这在极端情况下（比如 DAO 作妖）是个保底，但平时看着挺鸡肋。

最后说点人话

SSV 的问题是"技术牛逼，但收不到费，2026 年刚试着接上 ETH 的水管"；LDO 的问题是"水管早就铺好了，钱哗哗流，但告诉你这水和你没关系"。

买 LDO 本质上是在赌两件事之一：

要么你相信 Lido DAO 哪天真把 fee switch 打开或者大幅提高买回额度；

要么你认为 stETH 的网络效应无敌，即便 LDO 归零也不影响 stETH 的价值，所以拿 LDO 当个彩票玩。

我个人觉得，在 fee switch 有明确投票动向之前，LDO 很难摆脱"治理票根"的估值逻辑。180 亿美金的 TVL 撑得起 stETH，撑不起 3.4 亿美金 FDV 的 LDO，除非那 5% 的财库抽成真的开始往代币持有人身上流。

Ukraine says the Port of Greater Odesa is effectively shut down, putting pressure on grain exports

In recent days, reports about Ukraine’s Black Sea exit routes have heated up again. Ukraine has publicly stated that among the remaining Black Sea ports in the Greater Odesa area, operations are effectively shut down due to the impact of airstrikes. At the same time, several international shipping companies have tightened their berthing arrangements for the relevant ports. The incident also affects the timing of agricultural exports and global supply-chain expectations, and it is worth observing both the facts on the ground and the transmission pathways separately.

On the core facts, the Ukrainian government says that the remaining Black Sea ports in the Greater Odesa area are effectively closed in the context of airstrikes, and it signals that its planned agricultural exports could be cut in half, creating a risk to global grain supply. On the shipping side, the German container shipping company Hapag-Lloyd issued a customer notice stating that due to a worsening security situation in the Odesa area, the cooperating feeder service operators have stopped calling at Chornomorsk port, Odesa port, and Pivdennyi port (Southern Port). The corresponding feeder connections are paused, with the resumption time to be announced separately. Affected cargo may be diverted to other ports and transshipped, resulting in additional logistics costs. The company is assessing Renni port along the Danube as a preferred alternative discharge point, and if necessary, cargoes may also be rerouted to ports in Romania or Poland. Hapag-Lloyd made clear that the additional costs for port diversion, warehousing, and subsequent transport will be borne by the cargo-related parties, and that they will be handled according to the performance clauses affected on the bill of lading. Separately, industry reporting indicates that Maersk previously announced on July 22 that, due to rising Black Sea security risks, it would suspend related Chornomorsk routes indefinitely; some imported goods were redirected to the Port of Constanța in Romania.

What needs to be distinguished is this: a shipping line’s suspension of calls is not the same as all facilities being physically damaged. However, the official wording of “effectively closed,” combined with mainline carriers suspending services, indicates that port availability and commercial sailability have clearly declined.

In terms of logic, Black Sea ports are pivotal to Ukraine’s exports of agricultural products such as grains and oilseeds. If port operations are interrupted or feeder services are suspended, cargo flows get squeezed toward Danube ports, neighboring countries’ ports, and land-based intermodal transport—leading to a mismatch of shipping capacity, longer cycles, and higher costs. If export plans shrink significantly, supply expectations will first show up in grain and related agricultural trade; later, there will be knock-on adjustments in freight rates, insurance premium rates, and trade-financing conditions. Current information is sufficient to confirm two parallel facts—“officially recognized effective closure” and “head carriers pausing feeder services to the three ports”—but the final half-cut in exports, how long it will last, and the throughput capacity of alternative routes still depend on variables that have not been fully quantified, such as the security situation, port repairs, and the schedule of carriers resuming operations. Therefore, it should not be extrapolated directly as a certain outcome.

Impact pathways for the crypto market: the transmission is more indirect—through macro conditions and risk appetite—rather than a shock to the fundamentals of a single project. If the market interprets port disruptions as a global grain-supply disturbance, discussions about the stickiness of agricultural prices and broad inflation may intensify, which could then affect rate expectations and the pricing of risk assets. As geopolitical uncertainty rises, capital often first adjusts exposure to high-volatility assets; as one of the barometers of global risk appetite, the crypto market may therefore see correlated volatility. Another possible pathway is the rebalancing of dollar liquidity and risk-aversion sentiment: when expectations for commodity and shipping costs heat up, traders may reconsider how they allocate assets such as cash, precious metals, and Bitcoin. However, such mappings are typically lagging and unstable, and they may be offset by other macro data. Since crypto-native business has no direct contractual relationship with Black Sea ports, price volatility more likely reflects a sentiment premium and position management rather than a reassessment of cash flows.

Editor’s judgment and observations: the key incremental information in this round is that Ukraine’s official “effective closure” wording is mutually corroborated by international carriers suspending services, shifting the market narrative from “localized risk” to “export corridor blockage.” Going forward, three areas should be monitored closely: first, whether the Port of Greater Odesa shows any verifiable restart or one-way temporary passage arrangements; second, whether actual loading of agricultural cargoes and border transit data weaken in sync; third, whether the carrier notices expand the suspension from feeder services to broader insurance and rerouting clauses. Until evidence covers the specific tonnage affected, insurance quotes, and export deal details, it is more prudent to categorize the event as a supply-chain and macro-sentiment disturbance, rather than equating short-term rumors with a long-term collapse in supply. For crypto readers, a more practical approach is to observe it within a geopolitics—commodities—liquidity linkage framework, rather than mapping it to a single token story.

#乌克兰称敖德萨黑海港口实际关闭 #BTC #ETH #BNB

content:
乌克兰称大敖德萨港口实质关闭 粮出口承压

近期，围绕乌克兰黑海出海通道的消息再度升温。乌克兰方面公开表示，在大敖德萨地区剩余的黑海港口，受空袭影响已实质处于关闭状态；与此同时，多家国际航运企业也同步收紧了对相关港口的挂靠安排。事件同时牵动农产品外运节奏与全球供应链预期，值得从事实层面与传导路径上分开观察。

核心事实方面，乌克兰政府称，大敖德萨地区剩余黑海港口在空袭背景下实质上已关闭，并提示其计划中的农产品出口可能减半，进而对全球粮食供应构成风险。航运侧，德国集装箱航运公司赫伯罗特发布客户通知，称因敖德萨地区安全形势恶化，合作支线运营商已停止挂靠乔尔诺莫斯克港、敖德萨港与皮夫登尼港（南方港），相关支线连接暂停，恢复时间另行通知。受影响货物可能改港、转运，并产生额外物流成本；公司正在评估多瑙河沿岸雷尼港作为优先替代卸货点，必要时亦可能改至罗马尼亚或波兰港口。赫伯罗特明确，改港、仓储及后续运输等额外费用由货方利益相关方承担，并依据提单中影响履约条款处理。另据行业转述，马士基此前已因黑海安全风险上升，于7月22日宣布无限期暂停乔尔诺莫斯克相关航线服务，部分进口货调整至罗马尼亚康斯坦察港处理。需要区分的是：船公司暂停挂靠并不等同于所有设施物理损毁，但“实质关闭”的官方表述叠加主流船东停航，说明港口可用性与商业可航性已明显下降。

逻辑拆解上，黑海港口对乌克兰谷物、油籽等农产品出口具有枢纽意义。港口作业中断或支线停运，会把货流挤压到多瑙河港、邻国港口及陆路联运，带来运力错配、周期拉长与成本上移。出口计划若显著收缩，供给预期会先在粮食与相关农产品贸易中体现；再往后，才是运价、保险费率与贸易融资条件的连锁调整。当前信息足以确认“官方认定实质关闭”与“头部船东暂停三大港支线”两项并行事实，但出口最终减半幅度、持续时长及替代通道吞吐能力，仍取决于安全局势、港口修复与船东复航节奏，属于尚未被充分量化的变量，不宜直接外推为确定性结果。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多是宏观与风险偏好层面的间接传导，而非单一项目基本面冲击。若市场把港口受阻解读为全球粮食供应扰动，可能推升对农产品价格与广义通胀黏性的讨论，进而影响利率预期与风险资产定价；地缘不确定性上升时，资金往往先调整高波动资产敞口，加密市场作为全球风险偏好晴雨表之一，可能出现联动波动。另一条路径是美元流动性与避险情绪的再平衡：商品与航运成本预期升温时，交易者会重新权衡现金、贵金属与比特币等资产的配置逻辑，但这类映射通常滞后且不稳定，且会与其他宏观数据相互抵消。加密原生业务本身与黑海港口并无直接合同关系，因此价格波动更可能体现为情绪溢价与仓位管理，而非现金流重估。

编辑判断与观察：本轮信息的关键增量，在于乌克兰官方“实质关闭”表述与国际船东停航形成相互印证，使市场从“局部风险”切换到“外运通道受阻”叙事。后续应重点跟踪三方面：一是大敖德萨港口是否出现可核验的复航或单向临时通行安排；二是农产品实际装船与边境过境数据是否同步走弱；三是船东通知是否从支线暂停扩大到更广保险与绕航条款。在证据尚未覆盖具体停运吨位、保险报价与出口成交明细前，把事件定位为供应链与宏观情绪扰动更为稳妥，不宜把短期传闻直接等同于长期供给坍塌。对加密读者而言，更务实的做法是把它放入地缘—商品—流动性的联动框架中观察，而不是单点映射到某个代币故事。

title: 📉 彻底松动！交易员不再百分百定价美联储今年加息，2027年中前最多仅一次
subTitle:
#交易员下调2027年中前美联储加息押注 
当地时间8月14日，随着美国7月零售销售数据意外下滑，利率交易员进一步削减了对美联储的加息押注。根据CME FedWatch工具显示，市场对美联储9月会议加息的概率已降至34.8%，维持利率不变的概率高达65.2%。更值得注意的是，交易员已不再完全定价美联储今年会加息。
而在更长的期限上，交易员减少了对美联储在2027年中期前加息超过一次的押注，目前普遍预计美联储在2027年中前最多仅加息一次。
🔍 押注发生了什么变化？
回顾今年以来的利率预期演变，这一转变的幅度相当惊人：
· 从“两次以上”到“最多一次”：此前市场曾一度定价美联储今年加息次数有望达到2次乃至更多。而如今，到年底的利率收紧幅度已降至约23个基点——已不足一次加息所需的25个基点。
· 9月加息概率从“五五开”到34.8%：7月底时，9月加息概率尚处于“五五开”附近。一周前（8月7日左右）这一概率仍高达55%。CPI数据公布后降至约42%，PPI数据公布后进一步降至40%，零售销售数据出炉后最终定格在34.8%。
· 12月合约的彻底逆转：12月利率合约在过去几个月均完全计入了美联储今年加息的预期。但如今，市场对削减加息幅度的利率衍生品对冲工具需求强劲，尤其是针对明年3月到期合约的配置意愿尤为明显。
📊 为什么会出现这一转变？
1. 油价回落，通胀预期降温
自美国2月底袭击伊朗并引发供应冲击以来，国际基准油价一直是影响利率预期的重要因素之一。周四，随着交易员研判冲突释放的各种信号，油价下跌超过2%，进一步强化了市场对美国通胀已经见顶的乐观预期。
2. 通胀数据接二连三地温和
本周公布的CPI和PPI数据双双指向通胀降温：
· 7月CPI：整体符合预期，同比3.4%，环比0.1%
· 7月PPI：同比上涨4.7%，低于市场预期的4.9%，也低于6月5.5%的较大涨幅；环比持平，低于市场预期的上涨0.2%
3. 零售销售意外下滑，经济动能担忧升温
8月14日公布的美国7月零售销售数据环比下降0.6%，而市场预期为增长0.1%，前值为增长0.2%。这是自去年5月以来的最大降幅。消费这一支撑美国经济增长的重要引擎显现疲态，进一步削弱了加息的紧迫性。
📈 市场如何反应？
利率预期的松动在各大资产市场引发了连锁反应：
· 美债收益率全面走低：2年期美债收益率跌5.24个基点报4.140%，5年期跌6.71个基点报4.311%，10年期跌5.16个基点报4.639%，30年期跌3.96个基点报5.217%
· 金银上涨：贵金属在利率预期降温的背景下获得提振
· 美元承压：荷兰合作银行资深外汇策略师Jane Foley表示，美联储加息臆测近期因美国最新数据发布而受挫，为美元进一步走软开启了可能性
🏛️ 机构怎么看？
各大投行对美联储路径的判断仍存在分歧：
· 高盛：预计美联储2026年全年维持利率不变，首次降息要等到2027年6月和12月
· 摩根大通：此前预计首次加息在2027年下半年，但7月已将加息预期提前至2026年12月
· 东吴证券：预计2026年第三季度剩余的通胀数据将延续降温趋势，2027年第二季度美国通胀有望回归2%以下，维持美联储今年不加息的观点
Aegon Asset Management投资经理Colin Finlayson的评论很能代表市场情绪：“前几周市场还在剧烈争论沃什主席抗通胀的决心以及他是否会重启紧缩；但本周连番落地的通胀数据，无疑为这场论战泼了一盆冷水。”他进一步表示：“基于我们眼下掌握的数据，再谈论加息就显得有些不合时宜了。”
不过，鹰派声音并未完全消失。克利夫兰联储主席哈马克周四重申，鉴于通胀率自2021年以来始终高出2%的政策目标，她依然坚信加息具备合理性。
🔗 对加密市场意味着什么？
对于加密市场而言，利率预期的松动传递了多重信号：
· 宏观压力缓解：一个稳定的利率环境消除了此前持续压制数字资产的关键宏观逆风。比特币和其他风险资产在激进紧缩周期中历来表现挣扎，而当货币政策趋于稳定或宽松时则往往反弹。
· 但并非“全面鸽派”：9月加息34.8%的概率意味着市场并未完全排除美联储行动的可能性。一份超预期的通胀数据仍可能迅速重新定价预期，将加息概率推回高位。
· 高利率仍是“新常态”：高盛预计首次降息要到2027年下半年才到来，这意味着当前利率水平可能再持续一年或更久。对BTC、ETH等风险资产而言，估值修复的空间仍然受到制约。

从“年内加息两次以上”到“今年可能一次都没有”，再到“2027年中前最多仅一次”——市场对美联储路径的预期在短短几周内经历了剧烈重构。

ETH is around 1883 now. It’s been grinding for two days and still sits at this price. The news flow is all good, but at this level I’m not chasing longs.

In the past 24 hours, there’s been no shortage of ETH developments: ETF flows, staking products, institutional access, and even someone suggesting growth could be capped at around 0.4%, with forum sentiment also scoring fairly high. But what about the price? In the tight range of 1863–1890, it’s been moving back and forth like it’s caught in a small box. Both the daily and 4H charts are flat, and the trading volume is only about 50–60% of usual. One good catalyst after another, yet the price doesn’t budge. What’s missing isn’t the story—it’s actual money.

As for the money part, I’m even more uneasy. Spot large orders show net outflows totaling more than 60,000 ETH across roughly the last 5 candles. In the most recent three hours—over 12 candles—11 are net outflows. The spot market’s active order flow is also clearly skewed toward selling. On the futures side, it looks like active buy share is over 60%, but open interest isn’t rising; it feels more like short-term turnover rather than fresh capital entering. When spot is shrinking while futures are being played, that kind of divergence is usually not something I dare to chase.

Next, positions. Across all accounts, 71% are long. But for large holders, the proportion of long positions is actually declining. In big-wallet positions, longs are only a bit under 60%—retail traders are more optimistic than whales. Bullish sentiment isn’t low, but the “catching” money hasn’t followed. And ATR is already quite elevated; when it’s finally time to choose a direction, volatility will likely be amplified.

So my stance is simple: don’t chase—wait and watch. Let’s see whether spot large-order outflows can stop, whether trading volume can return, and whether 1890 can break and stand above on increased volume. Once at least one of those shows up, we can talk. Chasing longs here doesn’t offer good value—wait for the capital to show its intent first.

英伟达披露持有SpaceX近210亿美元股份

根据公开申报信息，英伟达披露了其重要股权投资组合中的两项大额持仓。截至第二季度末，该公司持有的SpaceX股份估值约为209.7亿至210亿美元；同期，其持有的英特尔股份估值约为300亿美元。上述数据来自监管申报与多家媒体对申报文件的转述，构成此次讨论的核心事实，也让市场重新审视芯片龙头在人工智能产业链上下游的资本布局方式。

更细的持股结构显示，英伟达持有SpaceX约1.228亿股A类股份。有报道称，SpaceX已于6月完成首次公开募股；若按相关报道提及的近期交易价格粗略匡算，该批股份对应市值较季度末账面估值有所回落。与SpaceX并列被披露的，是英伟达对英特尔的持股：第二季度末估值约300亿美元，其后随股价波动变化；另有表述指，英伟达在不到一年前向英特尔投资约50亿美元，使英特尔相关仓位成为其对外股权配置中的重要组成部分。股东排名方面，有数据称英伟达在SpaceX投资者中位居前列，但规模仍明显低于创始人埃隆·马斯克及Alphabet等主要持有人。以上数字均对应特定报告时点，不能直接外推为当前实时市值。

关于SpaceX股份如何进入英伟达资产负债表，媒体援引知情人士的路径描述是：英伟达在1月参与马斯克旗下xAI约200亿美元融资、出资约100亿美元；2月，SpaceX以约1.25万亿美元估值收购xAI，股权因此发生重组与映射。管理层沟通层面，马斯克在季报电话会中表示，SpaceX将在人工智能数据中心和先进模型中独家使用英伟达芯片，并预计明年获得“大量”新一代图形处理器。需要强调的是：申报文件确认的是持股数量与季度末估值等静态信息；融资换股路径、排他性供应表述以及IPO后市值波动，分别来自媒体转述或口头沟通，属于不同证据层级，存在口径差、条件条款与执行不确定性，不应与已全部落地的长期合同义务混为一谈。

从逻辑上看，英伟达此举更像“卖铲人”向下游算力场景与流量入口的深度绑定：一边通过英特尔等半导体资产保留产业协同弹性，一边借助SpaceX与xAI链路切入太空、能源与大规模训练基础设施叙事。对上市公司而言，大额股权既可能贡献投资收益与生态卡位，也会带来公允价值波动、信息披露与集中度风险。对一级与二级市场参与者而言，关键不在于单一新闻标题的冲击力，而在于这些股权是否转化为可持续的订单、供应份额与资本开支能见度。

映射到加密市场，直接影响路径并不直线。英伟达处于全球AI算力供给的中枢位置，其资本开支指引、大客户绑定和股权协同，往往先影响风险资产对“人工智能长期需求”的置信度，再传导至与算力租赁、分布式资源、模型应用相关的加密板块情绪；马斯克生态的任何产业进展，也可能短暂扰动与其个人品牌高度相关的主题代币关注度。然而，英伟达持有SpaceX或英特尔股份，本身并不改变公链结算、稳定币流通或协议费用等加密原生基本面，价格映射多以情绪和流动性为主，强度、时滞与持续性都不确定，不能把股权估值波动简单等同于某类代币的价值重估。

编辑判断是：这条披露的信息量，主要在于确认芯片巨头正用股权纽带加固AI基础设施同盟，而不是提供可交易的短线信号。后续更应跟踪正式财报附注、监管文件更新、SpaceX上市后的锁定期与减持约束，以及所谓独家芯片合作是否转化为可验证交付。把事实、转述和管理层展望分开看待，有助于避免在叙事拥挤阶段放大单一数据点的含义。

TSMC keeps soaring, and the chip shortage has made institutions nervous
TSMC’s valuation issues are becoming prominent as the company continues to see strong growth driven by robust chip demand, raising concerns in the market about increased volatility in the semiconductor sector.

Simply put, TSMC’s run-up is a bit excessive. Global chip demand is still just as strong—this Taiwan-based company’s orders are booked for the foreseeable future, and its share price has been going crazy as well. But here’s the question: is such a massive market cap really justified? Other tech stocks like Nvidia and AMD haven’t moved much, while TSMC keeps rallying and “reveling” in its own gains—that’s not normal. Reports say the reason behind this is that the market is worried about geopolitical risks (such as Taiwan’s security) and that the supply chain is too fragile; if something happens, the entire semiconductor industry could suffer.

Market impact
- Short term: Bitcoin and Ethereum likely won’t have any direct reaction, but other tech stocks may be sold off to some extent, since everyone is thinking about risk parity. Within the chip sector, besides TSMC, other companies may also be influenced by sentiment.
- Medium term: If TSMC’s valuation can hold steady, it suggests investors remain bullish on the tech industry long term, and capital will continue flowing here. But if the valuation gets knocked down, the entire tech sector could be dragged lower—because right now, when people look at tech stocks, their first reaction is to read TSMC’s “face.”

I think TSMC’s rally is a bit out of control, but considering that chips truly are in short supply, it may still stay firm in the near term. ECB Report: European Merchants Barely Use Crypto Payments
The ECB finds that cryptocurrencies account for only 0.2% of online payments, with even lower usage in physical stores—acceptance is extremely low, especially compared with the rise of mobile payments.

The European Central Bank has just released a report showing that across the entire euro area, the share of cryptocurrency for online payments is only 0.2%, and in physical stores it’s even lower—less than 1%. This sharply contrasts with the explosive adoption of mobile payments. In simple terms, merchants simply don’t care about cryptocurrencies. They’d rather use existing mobile payment systems than accept crypto. This data throws cold water on the outlook for crypto payments in Europe, suggesting that even with looser regulation, if merchants can’t use it or find it inconvenient, crypto is still unlikely to go mainstream.

Impact on the Market
- Short term: Bitcoin and Ethereum may face slight downward pressure from this news, because payment use cases are so crucial. If even merchants don’t use it, there’s less room for imagination about its value. Funds may first move out of payment-related tokens.
- Medium term: This further strengthens regulators’ determination to apply categorized oversight to crypto payments. If payments don’t work, they can’t be lumped together with traditional finance. The industry landscape may become even more fragmented, and only those payment solutions that truly solve merchants’ pain points will survive.

My Take
For cryptocurrencies to truly enter everyday life, payments are the hurdle you can’t get around. The fact that European merchants use crypto so little suggests that either the technology is too difficult, the costs aren’t worth it, or the risk is too high. Either way, my view is that for the $ETH rebound to hold above 1.9K, we need to see more tangible payment deployment scenarios—not just trading on hype. If the payment side keeps failing to take off, then no matter how high the price goes, it will still be a fleeting moment.

Switzerland’s largest online bank vents: crypto unit loses money and full-year revenue outlook is cut
Swissquote, a Swiss online bank, has lowered its full-year revenue guidance after a 66.2% drop in crypto-related income. This comes despite a 19.8% rise in client assets to a record high of $118.4 billion.

Swissquote’s client assets were up 19.8% year-on-year in the first half, reaching an astonishing $118.4 billion, which suggests people still place strong trust in this platform. However, the problem lies with the cryptocurrency business—an area that was expected to generate substantial profits. In the first half of this year, it actually recorded a 66.2% loss. What does that mean? Essentially, last year the company might still have been able to make a little money, but this year it is now taking a direct loss of nearly two-thirds. The original report didn’t specify exactly how much it lost, but with such a massive decline, it likely put serious pressure on company leadership.

Why did it lose so much? To be honest, weak market conditions are one factor. More importantly, crypto regulation is becoming stricter, which has shaken customer investment confidence. On top of that, there may be issues with the company’s own crypto business model. In short, a combination of factors has weighed down this segment. As a result, the company was forced to lower its full-year revenue outlook. While the report didn’t state by how much, it’s clear the company has little confidence in the crypto business right now.

Impact on the market
- Short term: This news is definitely a negative for crypto market sentiment, especially for crypto activities in Europe. Some may believe that even Switzerland’s largest online bank can’t hold up, raising questions about whether European regulation is truly coming. It could trigger some “safe-haven” capital to exit crypto, putting short-term pressure on the prices of BTC and ETH. In terms of fund flows, more capital may move toward traditional assets as a hedge.
- Medium term: Large financial institutions like Swissquote turning bearish on crypto could affect the industry’s overall development expectations. Over the coming months, if the crypto market continues to underperform, it may accelerate an industry shakeout. The expectation of tighter regulation will further strengthen, and for projects that don’t truly have real strength, it’s an end-of-the-road scenario.

My take
I’m bearish on the crypto market in the short term, especially ETH. With ETH trading around 1.88K, it will very likely test the 1.8K support level in the near term. If that breaks, 1.6K below is a key line of defense. Even a top-tier online bank like Swissquote can’t prop up its crypto business, which suggests the market may be at a critical moment.

Ethereum's Glamsterdam targets a 200M gas limit and up to 70% less MEV — but the "end of August" date being quoted is not locked.

The bull case: this is the most substantial change to $ETH since the Merge, and the contents are real. EIP-7732 enshrines proposer-builder separation, moving block construction on-chain and cutting MEV extraction by up to 70%. EIP-7928 adds block-level access lists for parallel transaction processing, lifting the gas limit from 60M toward 200M. EIP-7904 reprices gas with a targeted fee cut near 79%. It reached final devnet testing in June.

The bear case is the calendar, and it is being misreported. End of August is an internal working target, not a scheduled activation — no mainnet date is locked. Holesky and Hoodi must fork first and hold stable across multiple epochs, and recent forks needed two to four months of public-testnet seasoning. Ethereum Foundation contributors have said Glamsterdam is proving trickier and slower than Fusaka, which shipped in December. September to December is the firmer base case. Treat the specs the same way: 200M gas and 10,000 TPS are design targets, not launch numbers.

Our read: the engineering is the strongest part of Ethereum's roadmap in years, and the date is the weakest part of the coverage. Falsifiable — if Holesky and Hoodi fork cleanly within weeks, an autumn mainnet is credible. If testnets slip past September, this lands in Q4 or later and anyone positioned for an August catalyst is early by a quarter.

title: BTC真正的利好来了？别急着看“降息”，市场正在交易另一件更重要的事
subTitle:
最近BTC一直困在6.3万美元附近，但华尔街正在发生一个比短线K线更重要的变化：
市场对美联储继续加息的信心，正在松动。
最新公布的美国7月零售销售环比下降 0.6%，不仅低于市场此前预期的增长0.1%，也是9个月以来首次下降；更值得注意的是，用于GDP计算的重要核心销售指标也下降 0.4%。
与此同时，美国7月CPI同比从3.5%降至 3.4%，核心CPI同比进一步放缓至 2.5%。
这两个数据放在一起，市场看到的其实是一个非常关键的组合：
通胀正在降温，消费也开始降温。
这意味着美联储继续加息的门槛正在越来越高。
最新利率定价显示，9月加息概率已经下降至约三成左右。换句话说，市场正在从此前的“美联储还要继续收紧”，重新切换到：
“也许可以先停下来看看。”
而对于BTC来说，这才是真正值得关注的地方。
为什么？
因为过去压制BTC的核心因素之一，从来不只是“利率高”，而是市场不断担心：
实际利率继续升高 → 美元流动性进一步收缩 → 无风险收益率提高 → 资金继续远离高波动资产。
一旦加息预期持续下降，这条压制风险资产的链条就会开始松动。
但这里有一个非常反常的现象。
宏观环境开始改善，BTC为什么没有大涨？
截至目前，BTC仍然只有约 62,900美元，本周从约65,000美元重新回落，64,000美元上方的突破也没有成功延续。
这说明现在的市场存在一个非常明显的背离：
宏观边际利好正在出现，但加密市场自己的增量资金却没有跟上。
这可能比单纯看涨或者看跌更加重要。
美国股票基金截至8月12日当周已经重新获得约 25.8亿美元净流入，成长型股票基金更获得约 87.8亿美元净流入。也就是说，风险偏好并没有完全消失。
但BTC这边呢？
美国现货BTC ETF：
8月13日净流出约1.31亿美元；
8月14日继续净流出约5620万美元。
连续的资金撤离，恰恰解释了为什么宏观利好出现以后，BTC依然站不上64,000美元。
所以我认为，现在最大的误区就是看到“加息概率下降”，马上得出“BTC牛市重新启动”的结论。
真正完整的逻辑应该是：
经济降温
↓
继续加息概率下降
↓
短端金融条件边际改善
↓
风险资产估值压力缓解
↓
资金开始寻找高Beta资产
↓
ETF与现货增量资金重新流入
↓
BTC突破关键压力
现在我们只走到了前面几步。
最后、也是最关键的一步——资金回流，还没有出现。
这也是为什么BTC目前的6.3万美元区域，我反而认为非常值得观察。
如果接下来出现：
**BTC重新站稳64,000—65,000美元
ETF从持续流出转为连续净流入美债短端收益率进一步回落**
那么这轮上涨的性质就会发生变化。
届时它不再只是“数据刺激下的反弹”，而可能成为市场重新交易全球流动性改善的开始。
反过来，如果宏观利好不断出现，BTC却依然无法突破64,000—65,000美元——
那就需要提高警惕。
因为市场最弱的状态，从来不是“出了利空就跌”，而是：
出了利好，都涨不动。
这也是我现在对BTC最核心的判断：

A deal worth 128 million in a single transaction, and the price got smashed down to 0.1747.

In the past, I always thought stop-loss meant admitting defeat.

If you lose, it means you were wrong—cutting losses is basically admitting you’re stupid.

Later I realized: stop-loss is actually buying insurance.

That small loss you take buys you the right to bet again tomorrow.

If you don’t set a stop-loss, it’s like putting your entire account on a single judgment.

Today, $ACE is falling like this: -27.48%.

But at least the ones who cut losses are still alive.

The truly dangerous ones are those who hold on until the account gets carried all the way to zero.

Stop-loss has never been failure—it’s the way you leave yourself an exit.

That little loss can be considered the premium the market collects.

Next time I take the thread, will I dare to buy insurance again?

#dusk $DUSK In the same network, two completely different ledger systems run in parallel. This is the DuskDS documentation—it’s done quite well.

The first time I saw it, I was genuinely stunned.1 This design is great.

In Dusk’s DuskDS documentation, it’s explained very clearly: it supports two transaction models—Moonlight and Phoenix.

Moonlight is account-based and public. Balances are visible, and transfers show the sender, the recipient, and the amount. It fits scenarios that need public observation, such as financial reporting or compliance disclosures.@Dusk_Foundation 

Phoenix is UTXO-based and shielded. Funds exist in the form of encrypted “notes,” not in plain visible balances. Transactions are verified with zero-knowledge proofs that confirm “no double-spending” and “sufficient balance,” but they do not reveal the amount, the sender (except the recipient), or the specific notes.#ETH 

In the same network, both ledger systems run side by side. Ordinary users can go public if they want, or keep it private if they want—switch with a single click.

The subtle part of this design is that Moonlight and Phoenix can be converted into each other. If you send money from a public account to a shielded account, the money moves from the account system into the notes system—this conversion itself is a single Moonlight public transaction, but once it enters Phoenix, it disappears.

If a large amount of funds is transferred from Moonlight to Phoenix, the public ledger can only show that “the money went in,” but who it went to and how much—outsiders have no way of knowing. This leaves room for compliance, but it also creates blind spots for tracking. I believe once this dual-ledger setup works smoothly,$DUSK  it will reach an even higher level

content:
#dusk $DUSK 同一个网络里跑着两套完全不同的账本系统，这就是DuskDS文档，整的挺好

我第一次看到确实愣了一下1这设计很棒。

Dusk的DuskDS文档里写得很清楚：它支持两种交易模型——Moonlight和Phoenix。

Moonlight是账户制、公开的。余额可见，转账显示发送方、接收方和金额。适合需要公开观察的场景，比如财务报告或合规披露。@Dusk_Foundation 

Phoenix是UTXO制、屏蔽的。资金以加密"票据"形式存在，不是明余额。交易用零知识证明验证"没有双花、余额足够"，但不暴露金额、发送方（接收方除外）、以及具体票据。#ETH 

同一个网络，两种账本系统并行跑。普通用户想公开就公开，想隐私就隐私，一键切换。

这个设计的微妙之处在于：Moonlight和Phoenix之间可以互转。 你从公开账户往屏蔽账户打钱，钱从账户体系进入票据体系——这个转换本身是一笔Moonlight公开交易，但进入Phoenix之后就消失了。

如果大量资金从Moonlight往Phoenix转移，公开账本上只能看到"钱进去了"，但进了谁的口袋、有多少，外面的人根本不知道。这为合规留下了空间，但也制造了追踪的盲区。我相信只要这个双账本跑通,$DUSK 会更上一层楼

今晚以太是一根"横到下不去、也弹不起来"的死水线。日内高低 1886 / 1874.6，振幅不到 0.7%，收 1877.86，24h 只涨了 0.017%——基本原地踏步。量能 25.2 亿 USDT，比昨天 BTC 那一波带动的量级缩得明显，说明这地方多空都不想先动手，市场在等一个能把 1880 这个整数口撕开的方向。

📊 技术面
三个周期拆开看，节奏是"日线还撑着、4h 被压头、1h 在磨底"。1h 最没劲：价格 1877.86 卡在 MA7(1879.05)、MA25(1878.89) 两道之间来回蹭，MA50(1880.57)、MA99(1883.28) 全在头顶，RSI14 只有 48.2 中性偏弱，MACD 柱 -0.21 绿柱还在零轴下方小幅张口，小时级就是一根横盘线，没有方向。4h 才是今晚最该盯的：价格被 MA7(1880)、MA25(1882.78)、MA99(1887.88)、MA50(1895.68) 四道死死压在脚下，RSI14 掉到 34 接近超卖，MACD 柱 +0.31 刚有收窄翻红迹象但 DIF(-3.66) 还贴在零轴下方，属于"跌了一波后的弱势反抽、均线带没收回"的中继结构，1895 这道 4h MA50 是这轮短线命门。日线最关键也最稳：MA7(1883.87)、MA25(1891.39) 已经压在头上，但 MA50(1830.87) 还在脚下托着、MA99(1871.8) 也守住了，RSI14 还有 58.4 偏强，MACD 柱 -5.91 红柱转绿正在缩口——长线那轮从 1600 拉起来的修复结构没破，但 1900 整数口连续几天没回得去，日线大结构在慢慢磨顶。

关键位划死：上方 1883.87（日 MA7）+ 1891.39（日 MA25）是第一道坎，今晚连 1886 日内高都摸不回 1890，过不去就是弱；再上 1895.68（4h MA50）是短线命门，拿下才谈重新回到 1900 上方震荡。下方 1871.8（日 MA99）+ 1874.6 日内低是命门叠区，回踩不破才认横盘有效；真跌破 1871，下一档就看 1830.87（日 MA50），那是这轮修复最实质的防线，破了中线就该重新谈 1800 下方。

💧 衍生品与链上
永续资金费率 0.00004619（8h，约日化 0.014%），微正不热，多头没上头、空头也没逼空，双方都冷静。未平仓 2,355,813 ETH（约 44.2 亿 USDT），持仓不低，说明这波横盘是真有仓位在守，不是空拉。多空账户比最扎眼：多头账户占 71.84%、多空比 2.55，账面一边倒看多但价格不动，这种结构下插针扫多最容易打掉追着情绪进的杠杆。ETH/BTC 挂在 0.029811，相对 BTC 没明显走强也没崩，属于跟着大饼一起横的被动局。链上这块实时精确数字（质押率、Gas、ETF 净流量）公开通道今天拉不到，不瞎编；但从费率中性、OI 偏高但没到极端看，没有大规模清算或资金外逃信号，Fear&Greed 偏冷区能和缩量横盘对上。

📰 消息面
实时新闻抓取通道当前不可用，抓不到直接砸/拉以太的单一硬催化，不编具体事件。能确认的是衍生品层面没异常：费率中性、多空比偏多但价格不动，更像是"技术面 1880 整数口博弈 + 资金观望"驱动，而非单条消息引爆。宏观上今晚风险情绪偏中性，以太这种高 beta 资产在没催化时弹性也起不来。

👉 我的看法
短线我把 ETH 读成"1880 整数口箱体 + 方向未选 + 等待催化"。今晚实质进展几乎没有，只是 1h 在 1878 一带磨、4h 还压在均线带下、日 MA99(1871.8) 兜底——这种"上不去、下不破"的局，我更倾向再晃一阵而不是立刻选方向。操作上，没仓的别在 1877 盲接，等两件事之一：要么放量站回 1883.87（日 MA7）且回踩不破，我才认短空缓和；要么回调到 1871.8-1874.6 叠区企稳再轻仓上车，胜率比现在盲动高。有仓的把止损挂在 1871（日 MA99）下方，多空比 2.55 偏多、OI 高，插针最易打掉杠杆多。中线只要日线稳站 1895.68（4h MA50）且 RSI 守住 50 上方，我才认中期结构翻多；下方 1871 不破就还是偏强区间，破了就重新打开往 1830 去的空间。仓位控小，这种窄幅局插针振幅比想象中狠。

关键位复盘：压力 1883.87 / 1891.39 / 1895.68；支撑 1871.8 / 1874.6 / 1830.87。

Etherealize CEO Sounds the Alarm: Wall Street’s Private Blockchain Drive May Be a “Competition for the Lowest Standards”
Etherealize CEO warns that private blockchains promoted by Wall Street may be exacerbating inefficient finance. By contrast, public chains like Ethereum offer better scalability and transparency solutions—which is good news for Ethereum.

The CEO of Etherealize, a company focused on decentralized finance infrastructure, was blunt in a statement: the private blockchain push now aggressively promoted by Wall Street is essentially a “competition for the lowest standards.” The outcome may be to preserve the inefficiencies of the existing financial system, rather than bring genuine innovation. He said that private chains can breed backroom dealings because they are not publicly transparent, while public chains like Ethereum are the direction for the future development of financial technology—thanks to their inherent scalability and openly transparent nature. The core of this debate is whether financial technology should move toward greater transparency and openness, or a more closed-off and higher-efficiency path (even if it means sacrificing transparency). Currently, it seems Wall Street’s mainstream stance is more inclined toward the latter.

Impact on the market
- Short term: This view may cause investors to reassess their confidence in private-chain projects, while also increasing attention on public-chain projects. In the short run, it could provide some bullish sentiment support for public-chain coins such as Ethereum, but it won’t be decisive. In terms of capital flows, some funds may shift from private-chain concept stocks to Ethereum and other application-oriented public chains.
- Medium term: This warning may affect the landscape of the financial technology industry over the next few years. If the market gradually comes to recognize the value of public chains, the position of public chains such as Ethereum may be further strengthened, while the advantages of private chains may be weakened. In terms of regulatory trends, regulators may pay closer attention to transparency and compliance issues related to private chains, which could create a more relaxed development environment for public chains like Ethereum.

My take
I think this view is worth careful consideration. Private chains do have advantages in certain scenarios—for example, internal enterprise use or situations that require a high degree of privacy. But in the long run, the trend in financial technology should be toward greater transparency and openness, so that it can truly drive innovation and efficiency improvements. Public chains such as Ethereum have inherent advantages in this regard, and if they can continue to enhance performance and user experience, their value will be further reflected. Of course, there will be many challenges along the way too, such as performance bottlenecks and regulatory uncertainties. But overall, I’m optimistic about the long-term development prospects of public chains like Ethereum—especially considering their broad applications in decentralized finance and non-fungible tokens (NFTs).

Etherealize CEO敲响警钟：华尔街私链运动可能是一场“底线竞争”
Etherealize CEO警告说，华尔街推动的私有区块链可能正在加剧金融效率低下，相比之下，以太坊等公链提供更优的扩展性和透明度解决方案，这对以太坊是好消息。

Etherealize这家专注于去中心化金融基础设施的公司CEO，在一份声明中直言不讳：华尔街现在大力推广的私有区块链，本质上是在搞一场“底线竞争”，结果可能就是维持现有金融体系的不效率，而不是带来真正的创新。他说私有链因为不公开透明，容易滋生暗箱操作，而以太坊这样的公链才是未来金融科技发展的方向，因为它天然具备可扩展和公开透明的特点。这场辩论的核心在于，金融科技是应该走得更透明、更开放，还是更封闭、更高效（即使牺牲透明度）的道路。目前华尔街的主流态度，似乎更倾向于后者。

对市场的影响
- 短期：这个观点可能会让投资者重新评估对私有链项目的信心，同时提升对公链项目的关注。短期内，可能会对像以太坊这样的公链币种产生一定的利好情绪支撑，但不会是决定性的。资金流向上，可能会有一部分资金从私有链概念股流向以太坊等实际应用型公链。
- 中期：这个警告可能会影响未来几年金融科技行业的格局。如果市场逐渐认同公链的价值，以太坊等公链的地位可能会进一步巩固，而私有链的优势可能会被削弱。监管趋势上，监管机构可能会更加关注私有链的透明度和合规性问题，这可能会给以太坊等公链带来更宽松的发展环境。

我的判断
我认为这个观点值得深思。私有链确实在特定场景下有优势，比如企业内部使用或者需要高度隐私的场景。但是从长远来看，金融科技的发展趋势应该是更加透明和开放，这样才能真正推动创新和效率提升。以太坊等公链在这方面具有天然优势，未来如果能够持续提升性能和用户体验，其价值会进一步体现。当然，这个过程中也会面临不少挑战，比如性能瓶颈、监管不确定性等。但总体来说，我看好以太坊等公链的长期发展前景，特别是考虑到其在去中心化金融、非同质化代币（NFT）等领域的广泛应用。

BTC $63,000 can’t break through anymore? Is the Fed being truly tough this time?

Since US inflation hasn’t fallen to target, the Fed has no reason to cut rates right away, so cryptocurrencies are bound to be affected.

Put simply, inflation data still hasn’t met expectations. In June, the inflation rate is still above 3%, higher than the Fed’s 2% target. This means the Fed still needs to keep up its tough stance, and the likelihood of rate cuts in the short term is low. Fed Chair Powell has also recently signaled that they will keep focusing on the data to decide next steps. For the market, this is basically a bucket of cold water. Crypto is the kind of asset that likes loose monetary policy—so now investors need to weigh things carefully.

US economic data has been mediocre overall, and inflation hasn’t shown a clear downward trend. That suggests the Fed will likely maintain high interest rates. This has a direct impact on global capital flows: people will worry about problems in the US economy, and risk assets—like crypto—are more likely to be hit. Part of the recent rise in Bitcoin and Ethereum is driven by hopes that the Fed will loosen policy. But now that expectation has failed, they will face pressure in the short term.

Market impact
- Short term: Bitcoin and Ethereum may continue to trade in a range, and bearish sentiment could intensify. Funds may flow out of the crypto market and into bonds or other safe-haven assets. In the short term, $63,000 is a key resistance level for Bitcoin. If it can’t hold, price could drop toward $60,000. Ethereum at $1,879.53 is also under notable pressure; if it breaks below $1,750, it may then test support around $1,600.

- Medium term: If the Fed’s stance is truly hardline, crypto will need more good news from the US economy to return to an upward trend. Also, rate cuts were originally an important reason the market expected crypto to rise—now that expectation is gone, which isn’t good for the long run. That said, crypto doesn’t fully move in lockstep with the Fed. Many funds are still looking at technicals and institutional behavior.

My take
I think it’s hard to be optimistic in the short term for both Bitcoin and Ethereum. If the Fed doesn’t cut rates, it’s like hitting pause on crypto’s upside momentum. The $63,000 level for Bitcoin must be defended; if it fails, there’s a risk of dropping to $60,000. The $1,879.53 level for Ethereum is similar: if it breaks below $1,750, it could continue sliding. However, it’s not absolutely bearish—if US economic data keeps deteriorating and the Fed turns earlier, crypto could still find an opportunity.

Stop blindly following trades! This proven crypto trading strategy has a win rate as high as 98.8%
1. Split capital to manage risk
Divide your funds into 5 parts and use only 1/5 of the position each time. Set a stop-loss at 10 points; even if you’re wrong on a trade, the loss is only 2% of total capital. You only reach a 10% loss after 5 consecutive mistakes. If your judgment is correct, set take-profit at 10 points or more to fundamentally reduce the risk of getting stuck in a bag.
2. Ride the trend to improve your win rate
To further raise the win rate, the key is “follow the trend.” In a downtrend, every rebound is often a bull-trap designed to lure you in; in an uptrend, every dip is often a golden opportunity to buy.
3. Avoid short-term blowout coins
Whether it’s a major coin or an altcoin, there are very few that can run multiple waves of a strong markup. After a short-term explosive rally, it becomes extremely difficult for the price to keep climbing. When a high-level rally stalls, it’s inevitable that the next move will be a decline due to lack of momentum.
4. Use MACD to judge entry and exit signals
Use MACD as an aid: when the DIF line crosses above the DEA below the 0-axis (a golden cross) and breaks through the 0-axis, it’s a solid entry signal. When MACD forms a death cross above the 0-axis and moves downward, cut down positions decisively to avoid giving back profits.
5. Refuse to “average down” into losses—only add to winners
“Averaging down” has ruined countless retail traders—further losses lead to further averaging down, and further averaging down leads to deeper losses, eventually trapping you in despair. Remember this iron rule: never average down when you’re losing; only add to your position when you’re in profit, so gains compound—not losses.
6. Volume and price are the soul—track where the money goes
Trading volume is the “barometer” of crypto capital, more reliable than simply looking at candlesticks. When the price breaks out from a low consolidation area with rising volume, focus on it. When you see high-level price stalling with heavy volume, it indicates the capital is weak at absorbing the selling pressure—exit decisively.
7. Only trade rising trends—don’t waste time
Prefer coins that are in an uptrend; the odds are higher and the efficiency is better. After each trading day, you must review: check whether your logic for holding coins has changed; confirm whether the trend matches your prediction by using weekly candlestick charts; and follow the timing to secure your entry.

#dusk  Bitcoin (#BTC ) or Ethereum (#ETH ) old hands should all know the traditional Gossip flood-broadcast protocol.
Today, I took a look at the Kadcast P2P protocol mentioned in the @Dusk_Foundation  ($DUSK ) whitepaper, and it feels quite enlightening— it directly turns this “shout in the square” approach into a “precise delivery” one.
In simple terms, Kadcast borrows the XOR-distance algorithm from the Kademlia hash table (DHT), arranging all network nodes into an ordered, tree-like topology based on their mathematical distances.
When a node needs to broadcast, it no longer blindly scatters messages; instead, like a relay delivery service, it cascades through the tree structure to precisely distribute the message to specific nodes. This brings several very intuitive changes in experience:
Ultra-low redundancy: nodes won’t repeatedly receive identical duplicate messages, and bandwidth consumption drops dramatically.
Lightning-fast coverage: the message spreads across the entire network instantly via multicast trees with the minimum number of relay hops.
Supports high-frequency finance: when node network resources are constrained or in high-frequency trading scenarios, it can guarantee very low latency and very high throughput.
But from a practical standpoint, structured networks also have potential downsides. If tree-topology nodes frequently go online and offline (churn), or if a critical relay node is targeted by a hacker DDoS attack, could broadcasts experience short-term gaps? Under extreme-market pressure testing, can this structure maintain a fault-tolerance rate as brutal yet resilient as Gossip? These still need to be validated in future mainnet high-concurrency scenarios.
What do you think—could a protocol like this that optimizes the P2P layer become standard for the next generation of financial public chains? Discuss in the comments!

#dusk  比特币（#BTC ）或者以太坊（#ETH ）的老玩家应该都知道传统 Gossip 洪泛广播协议。
今天看了看 @Dusk_Foundation  ($DUSK ) 白皮书里提到的 Kadcast P2P 协议，感觉它的解法很有启发性——它直接把这种“广场大喊大叫”改成了“精准快递派送”。
简单来说，Kadcast 借用了 Kademlia 哈希表（DHT）的 XOR 距离算法，把全网节点按数学距离编成了一棵有序的“树状拓扑图”。
当一个节点要发广播时，它不再盲目撒网，而是像快递接力一样，按树状结构级联（Cascading）精准分发给特定节点。这带来了几个很直观的体验变化：
冗余极低：节点不会反复收到相同的重复消息，带宽消耗直接砍掉一大截。
极速覆盖：消息通过多播树（Multicast trees）以最少的中继次数瞬间传遍全网。
支撑高频金融：在节点网络资源受限或者高频交易场景下，能保证极低的时延和极高的吞吐量。
不过从实战角度来看，结构化网络也是有隐患的。如果树状拓扑节点频繁上下线（Churn），或者某个关键中继节点被黑客 DDoS 攻击，广播会不会出现短暂断层？在极端行情的压力测试下，这种结构能否保持像 Gossip 那样野蛮但顽强的容错率？这些还需要未来主网高并发场景的检验。
你们觉得这种针对 P2P 底层优化的协议，能成为下一代金融公链的标配吗？评论区交流交流！

When the structure hasn’t changed, every rebound is a chance to reduce exposure—not a signal to add.

━━━ Discipline is worth more than predictions ━━━
Today, I won’t open any new trades. I’ll wait for the system-switch signal, for the RSI to repair, for the structure to speak. In an uncertain market, staying in cash is the position.

I’ve seen too many people bottom-fishing in a bearish system, only to miss the true bull market. The reason is simple: they’re trading with emotions, not with a system.

A common mistake is placing your stop-loss too far, which is basically the same as not having one; or placing it too close, so you get knocked out by a little fluctuation. A simple and straightforward rule of thumb: don’t set it beyond the maximum loss you can tolerate per trade. For example, if your principal is 10,000, and the most you can lose on a single trade is 2%, that’s 200. Then you need to work backward to calculate the leverage multiple and the stop-loss distance accordingly. Position sizing and stop-loss placement are a set—they shouldn’t be decided on a whim. First figure out how much you can afford to lose, then talk about how much you can make. DYOR—keep your hands under control. #ETH #止盈止损 #仓位管理 #交易策略 #Futures trading

title: Your Rules Before Your Emotions Take Over.
subTitle:
The hardest time to make a good investment decision is often when the market is moving fast. When prices are pumping, greed speaks. When prices are crashing, fear speaks. That's why disciplined investors don't wait for emotions to tell them what to do.
They establish their principles beforehand. Know your: Entry conditions. Risk tolerance. Position size. Time horizon. Reasons for exiting. Conditions that would invalidate your thesis. Then, when the market becomes emotional, you have something stronger to follow than the crowd.
🔑 Key Takeaway: A plan made in calm conditions can protect you from decisions made in emotional conditions. You don't need to predict every market move. You need to know how you will respond when the unexpected happens.
🧠 Practical Reflection; Before your next investment, ask yourself: "If the market moves sharply against me tomorrow, do I already know what I will do?" If you don't have an answer, perhaps the decision isn't ready yet.
Thought for the Day. Don't create your rules while you're under pressure. Create them before the pressure arrives.
Systems over emotion. Conviction over noise.

3x BTC/ETH ETFs are coming: If BTC rises 10%, do you definitely make 30%?
Cboe BZX has just filed an application to list a 3x Bitcoin ETF and a 3x Ether ETF. The name is exciting, but it’s also the easiest to misunderstand—especially the “3x.”
In one sentence: it targets 3x the daily percentage move, not a scenario where, after long-term holding, your total BTC returns are always multiplied by 3.
According to official documents, the 3x BTC ETF would gain exposure through tools such as CME Bitcoin futures, related ETPs/ETFs, and options; the ETH version follows a similar logic. The goal is for the fund to deliver 3x the underlying’s daily performance, before fees are deducted.
The real trap is the “daily reset.”
When the market moves strongly in one direction, a 3x leverage product can be very powerful; but if BTC repeatedly makes big up-and-down swings, even if it eventually returns to the original price, the 3x ETF may still result in losses due to compounding effects and volatility drag.
So this is more like wrapping leveraged derivatives exposure into a traditional brokerage/security account, rather than “buy it and hold until BTC rises threefold.”
What I think it really shows is: Wall Street is no longer satisfied with letting investors buy BTC directly—they’re now productizing the high volatility of crypto as well.
But don’t rush to look for code yet—this is currently just an application, not an approval to be listed.
#BTC  #ETH  #etf #cboe申请3倍比特币与以太坊etf

title: 📉 预期全错！美国7月零售销售环比暴跌0.6%，创去年5月以来最大降幅
subTitle:
#美国7月零售销售下降0.6% 
当地时间8月14日，美国商务部人口普查局公布的数据给了市场一记重锤：美国7月零售销售环比下降0.6%，创下2025年5月以来最大单月跌幅。而市场此前的普遍预期是增长0.1%——预期与实际之间相差了整整0.7个百分点。
📊 核心数据一览：
· 7月零售销售总额：7,636亿美元（季调后），环比-0.6%，预期+0.1%，前值+0.2%
· 剔除汽车后销售：环比-0.3%，预期+0.2%
· 剔除汽车与汽油后：环比-0.2%，预期+0.3%
· 核心零售（控制组）：环比-0.4%，预期+0.3%
各项核心指标全线不及预期。
📉 分项数据：几乎“全军覆没”
· 非门店零售（线上电商）：环比-2.2%——最大拖累项
· 机动车及零部件经销商：环比-1.8%
· 加油站：环比-0.9%（受油价下行拖累）
· 家电电子：环比-0.5%
· 服装店：环比+1.9%——为数不多的亮点
🔍 为什么跌得这么狠？
1. 亚马逊Prime Day提前：今年Prime Day从传统的7月提前到了6月，线上消费需求被提前透支。
2. 退税效应消退：2026年上半年大额个税退税带来的一次性消费刺激已完全结束。
3. 储蓄率跌至四年低点：居民预防性缓冲资金持续消耗，自由支配支出弹性大幅收缩。
4. 油价下行+天气因素：加油站营收受油价拖累，独立日前后高温天气也压制了线下消费意愿。
🏛️ 市场反应：加息预期再遭重锤
数据公布后，市场迅速反应：
· 美债收益率全面走低：两年期国债收益率一度被推低至4.10%下方，创6月30日以来最低；10年期收益率报4.629%。
· 美元走弱：美元指数回吐本周涨幅。
· 黄金大涨：现货黄金在数据公布前已提前上涨约15美元，公布后进一步快速上涨12美元，至4,381美元附近。
交易员进一步削减了加息押注——不再完全定价美联储今年会加息，对2027年中前加息超过一次的押注也大幅减少。
BMO资本市场美国利率策略主管Ian Lyngen直言：“这是一份关于消费者整体健康状况的令人不安的更新。”
🔗 对加密市场意味着什么？
零售数据公布后，比特币下跌1.51%。为什么“数据疲软→降息预期升温→利好风险资产”的经典逻辑这次没跑通？
1. 消费放缓引发经济担忧：消费占美国经济活动的约三分之二。当“经济软着陆”叙事受到挑战时，资金的第一反应往往是避险，而非拥抱风险资产。
2. 降息是把“双刃剑”：降息预期升温确实利好BTC、ETH等资产的长期估值逻辑，但如果降息是因为经济在恶化，短期的避险情绪会压过长远的利好。
3. BTC仍在区间震荡：目前比特币在62,000-66,000美元区间内反复拉锯。市场需要更多数据确认消费放缓是“暂时性”的还是“趋势性”的。
💡 怎么看？
7月零售数据同比仍增长5.0%，消费绝对规模依旧稳健。但这组数据释放的信号很清晰：支撑美国经济近两年的消费韧性，正在松动。
对加密市场而言，短期看情绪，中期看流动性。若后续就业、通胀数据继续降温，美联储政策转向的预期将进一步强化——那才是BTC、ETH真正受益的时候。
投资有风险，决策需谨慎。本文仅作信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Today I noticed the actions of @Dusk_Foundation  integrating with Chainlink CCIP. I didn’t monitor the price trend of $DUSK ; I just went straight to digging through the developer guide. Now there’s a deadly test for the RWA sector: when real-world assets move over to Ethereum, can “compliance review” actually be pierced through end-to-end?

Following the underlying logic, CCIP is responsible for locking and mapping assets on both ends, and it does support embedding custom rules. But the crux is that Moonlight’s identity verification only controls the outflow of funds. Once the tokens land on Ethereum, the receiving side has no idea about the recipient’s qualifications. Identity tags can’t just move around like crypto assets can. Either you bundle the screening results into the messaging protocol and send them over, or the receiving end has to redo the filtering from scratch. However, after digging through all the materials, there’s basically no sign of any “cross-chain identity inheritance” standard.

This directly exposes a weakness in NPEX’s €200–300M tokenized securities business. When it runs in a single chain, it’s watched by the Dutch AFM. But the moment multi-chain settlement is involved, partners would have to deploy audit traceability infrastructure that satisfies the strict requirements of MiCA and MiFID II on each major network. Before the home base platform is fully secured, rushing to bridge outward carries massive hidden risks.

To verify, I personally went to the Sepolia testnet and ran the experiment. I used a wallet that had been certified to transfer funds to a purely blank address. The funds went through smoothly within three minutes, with the risk controls effectively acting as if they weren’t there. This shows that today’s cross-chain bridges “just move money, but don’t verify people.”

In summary: until qualification/eligibility can be truly pierced through, simply praising the multi-chain narrative is not a solid argument. It’s better to wait and research once the project’s regulatory compatibility whitepaper is actually implemented. For now, blindly adding positions carries too much risk. #eth $ETH

translatedData.content:
#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  afternoon saw @Dusk_Foundation  connect to Chainlink CCIP, didn’t pay attention to $DUSK ’s market move, I went straight to dig through the developer docs. Everyone is talking about multi-chain, but I only care about one hard issue: can RWA assets move from Dusk to Ethereum with compliance tags seamlessly carried over?

According to the docs, CCIP uses Programmable Token Pools to handle locking and minting on both ends, and it allows inserting custom verification logic. The catch is this: Moonlight’s KYC can block funds from leaving the source chain. But once the coin is on Ethereum, how does the destination side recognize the identity of the recipient? Compliance proof isn’t the token itself, so it can’t be directly bridged. Either Dusk bundles the data packets and sends them over, or the receiving side has to redo the screening. I looked through the cross-chain communication specs and there isn’t any standard module for identity inheritance.

That directly chokes the neck of NPEX’s €200–300M tokenized securities platform. In single-chain mode, the Dutch AFM can still keep an eye on it, but once you do cross-chain settlement, your counterparty has to rebuild compliance interfaces and nodes across all networks. MiCA watches transaction records, MiFID II insists on auditability and traceability—this isn’t something you can just wave through by writing a few contracts. If the native chain infrastructure isn’t even fully running, then jumping into multi-chain expansion is basically building a floor without laying the foundation.

To verify, I went on a quick spin through the Sepolia testnet. Moonlight’s bridge took only about 3 minutes. I deliberately transferred from a KYC-certified wallet to a “blank slate” unverified address, and the tokens went through smoothly with no risk-control blocks. This confirms that compliance attributes don’t automatically follow—you have to hardcode it chain by chain.

In plain terms, cross-chain bridges just ship the goods; they don’t check IDs. The multi-chain story sounds rich, but implementation is still missing a piece. Until an explicit regulatory compatibility whitepaper is released, I wouldn’t recommend rushing in while everyone’s fired up. #eth $ETH

Bitcoin’s old wallet was hacked for $116 million, while ETFs are flowing back: why does no one seem to care?

💡 Negative: A dormant whale-wallet was drained of $116 million worth of BTC, putting self-custody security under the microscope and first hitting market sentiment.

The biggest security event this week: An old Bitcoin wallet that hadn’t moved in years was attacked, and hackers directly stole $116 million in BTC. These “sleeping whales” are always prime targets for hackers—they specifically go after signature and private-key vulnerabilities in old wallets. Ironically, the same week the news flow was relatively warm: Bitcoin ETF funds returned to net inflows, Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) said it plans to keep accumulating BTC, and mining companies are also chasing multi-billion-dollar AI compute orders. One sentence translation: Institutional players are doubling down, while retail users’ private keys are essentially left exposed. And the BTC price is still trading around $63,116—up only 0.29% over the past 24 hours—so the market barely reacts to such a large theft.

Impact on the market
Short term: Negative. The $116 million scale is enough for headlines. Historically, after this kind of incident, the market usually pretends it’s fine first, then follows with a drop. ETF inflows and Strategy’s buying act as a stabilizing force, but they can only prop up price—not sentiment. BTC has been grinding around the 63,000s for days without breaking higher, which itself is a sign of weak momentum. Once the stolen coins start moving on-chain and heading toward the market, the selling pressure becomes real.

Medium term: Self-custody security concerns will likely be repeatedly highlighted by the media and regulators. It’s not out of the question that someone will use this incident to push for even stricter custody rules, which would be a long-term hit to the decentralization narrative. Mining companies doing AI is a story for publicly listed firms in the U.S. stock market, and it helps BTC price only limitedly.

My view
I’m bearish in the short term. The logic is straightforward: If the stolen $116 million BTC is eventually “washed out” by the hackers, it becomes overhang supply—selling pressure hanging over the market. When price doesn’t react to bad news, it’s often not resilience; it’s negligence. First, BTC is watching the $62,000 support level—if it breaks, downside room opens. Until a rebound can reclaim above $64,500, treat it as weak consolidation. ETH around $1,885 follows the same linkage logic—don’t expect an independent move. Let the bullets fly a bit longer.

U.S. 30-year Treasury yields surge to 5.25%, with France, Germany, and Japan deteriorating at the same time: Why is this bad news for BTC?

Global long-term Treasuries are being sold off en masse, and borrowing costs are skyrocketing—bad for risk assets like BTC and ETH, and likely to face short-term pressure.

France’s 30-year government bond yield has jumped to nearly 4.85%. This is not just a problem for France—Germany, Japan, and the U.S. have also seen their long-term Treasuries hit at the same time. U.S. 30-year Treasury yields have touched around 5.25%, the highest level seen in many years.

In plain terms: global investors are collectively “voting with their feet.” Governments are borrowing too aggressively and deficits aren’t being brought under control. Holders of long-term government bonds demand higher compensation; otherwise, they won’t take the risk. This isn’t a problem limited to one country. The U.S., Europe, and Japan are all being “charged for fiscal policy” by the market, forcing governments to face borrowing costs.

One-sentence translation: previously cheap money is getting expensive—and it may not return to “cheap” in the short term.

Market impact

- Short term: Money runs toward the bond market and cash. With Treasury yields elevated, earning steady interest at the ~5% level is more attractive than holding volatile risk assets. Crypto is the first to feel it. BTC is currently at $63,063.82 and ETH at $1,883.64, moving only about 0.5% in 24 hours. It looks stable, but in reality both bulls and bears are reluctant to make the first move. If the bond market continues to worsen, tighter liquidity will hit risk assets first; crypto prices going sideways is the calm before the storm.
- Medium term: If long-term bond yields stay elevated for a long time and global liquidity shifts from loose to tight, the valuation logic for all risk assets will need to be repriced. COW short-term rebound is significant: nearly 50% up over 24 hours

CoW Protocol (token ticker: COW) saw a relatively large short-term rebound in the secondary market. Based on publicly available market data, the token recorded nearly a 50% gain over the past 24 hours, with gains also reaching more than 30% over the last week. After quickly lifting from a prior relative low range, trading activity increased in parallel. Similar to many small- and mid-cap assets that have been consolidating within a narrow range for a long time, this round of performance is first reflected in rising volatility and strengthened momentum, rather than a slow grind down or a gradual climb.

In terms of project positioning, CoW Protocol falls under decentralized trading infrastructure. Its core mechanism is not to have users trade directly on-chain against counter-parties instantly, but rather for users to sign swap intents, which are then sent to solvers to compete for the best execution path and complete settlement. The protocol emphasizes reducing path inefficiencies, gas, and slippage through batch matching and “order-flow coincidence.” When direct matching conditions are insufficient, it falls back to comparing quotes via mainstream aggregator routes. As a result, COW is more often categorized as a DEX-related asset with a real product narrative over the long run, rather than a short-lived hype driven purely by sentiment. Understanding this context helps place price volatility back into the framework of a “trading infrastructure token,” instead of looking only at the raw numbers for up/down performance.

As for the key facts of this round, what can be confirmed is that the short-term gain is substantial, the intra-day spread between high and low prices has widened, and market attention has returned. However, as of now, public materials are not sufficient to precisely attribute the rally to a single official positive catalyst that just occurred. In other words, the price increase is a verifiable market outcome, while the explanatory cause is still incomplete. A more reliable breakdown is as follows: when liquidity is still acceptable and traders’ risk appetite has temporarily recovered, targets with relatively limited circulating market caps and sustained product narratives are more likely to be selected first by short-term capital, leading to a volume-driven push higher. Once buy-side demand becomes crowded, the speed of price discovery is typically much faster than the speed at which information can be clarified. This is a common phenomenon at the level of trading structure, and it cannot be directly equated with an abrupt step-change in fundamentals.

Regarding how the crypto market is affected, the pathway can be viewed in roughly three layers. The first is the asset itself: rising hype increases spot turnover and may also transmit into related derivatives markets, amplifying volatility further—both the upside push and the pullback can accelerate. The second is sector mapping: narratives similar to intent trading, batch auctions, solver activity, or DEX efficiency optimization sometimes see sentiment spillover, but the strength of spillover depends on whether the main theme is resonating at that time. There is no inevitable rule that “one coin goes up and all coins in the same track automatically follow.” The third layer is the overall market relationship: a pulse in a single mid- or small-cap token more often reflects structural differentiation and a shift in capital preferences. It usually is not enough to independently rewrite the medium-term direction of mainline assets such as Bitcoin or Ethereum, but it may intensify high-to-low swings and theme rotation during fragile sentiment periods.

From the editor’s perspective, “a significant rebound that has already happened” and “a trend continuation not yet verified” should be strictly separated. A nearly 50% gain over 24 hours by itself implies that crowded short-term trading and pullback risk rise at the same time. If, going forward, there is no confirmation of sustained ecosystem data, product progress, or supply-side positives, the speed at which price returns to the prior consolidation range is often not slow. For observers, a more valuable set of follow-up indicators is not whether the single-day gain can expand further, but whether solver competition is becoming more active, whether the protocol’s real trading intents are increasing, whether token circulation and unlock schedules create supply pressure, and whether volume and price action match during the rebound. Interpret this round of行情 as a rapid price adjustment driven by a resonance between liquidity and momentum, rather than being overly eager to draw a one-sided conclusion. Market volatility cannot be preplanned, and information completeness is limited—so any interpretation should leave room for revision.

COW短线显著反弹 24小时涨幅近五成

CoW Protocol（代币代号COW）在二级市场出现一轮幅度较大的短线反弹。综合公开行情信息，该代币在24小时维度录得接近五成的涨幅，近一周涨幅也达到三成以上，价格自前期相对低位区间快速抬升，交投活跃度同步提高。与多数长时间窄幅整理后的中小市值资产类似，本轮表现首先体现为波动率抬升与动量强化，而非缓慢阴跌或阴涨式修复。

从项目定位看，CoW Protocol属于去中心化交易基础设施方向。其核心机制并不是让用户交易直接在链上即时对手成交，而是由用户签署互换意图，再交由求解器竞争最优执行路径并完成结算。协议强调通过批量撮合与“需求巧合”降低路径损耗、gas与滑点，并在缺乏直接撮合条件时回退到主流聚合路由比较报价。因此，COW长期更常被归类为带有真实产品叙事的DEX相关资产，而不是纯粹情绪驱动的短命题材币。了解这一背景，有助于把价格波动放回“交易基础设施代币”的框架里观察，而不是只看涨跌幅数字本身。

就本轮核心事实而言，能够确认的是短时涨幅显著、日内高低价差扩大，以及市场关注度回升；但截至目前，公开材料并不足以把涨势精确归因于某一条刚发生的单一官方利好。换句话说，涨幅是可核验的市场结果，驱动解释则仍不完整。更稳妥的拆解是：在流动性尚可、交易者风险偏好出现阶段性回暖时，流通市值相对有限、又具备持续产品叙事的标的，更容易先被短线资金选中，形成放量上冲；一旦买盘拥挤，价格发现速度会明显快于信息澄清速度。这属于交易结构层面的常见现象，不能直接等价为基本面已经发生阶跃。

对加密市场的影响路径，大致可分三层观察。第一层是标的自身：热度上升会提高现货换手，并可能向相关衍生品市场传导，使波动进一步放大，上冲与回撤都可能提速。第二层是板块映射：意图交易、批量拍卖、求解器或DEX效率优化等相近叙事，有时会出现情绪外溢，但外溢强度取决于当时主线是否共振，并不存在“一个币上涨、同赛道自动跟涨”的必然规律。第三层是大盘关系：单个中小市值代币的脉冲，更多反映结构分化和资金偏好切换，通常不足以单独改写比特币、以太坊等主线资产的中期方向，却可能在情绪脆弱阶段加剧市场的高切低与主题轮动。

编辑判断上，应把“已经发生的大幅反弹”和“尚未被验证的趋势延续”严格分开。接近五成的24小时涨幅，本身就意味着短期拥挤交易与回撤风险同步上升；若后续缺乏持续的生态数据、产品进展或供给层面的利好验证，价格向原整理区间回归的速度往往并不慢。对观察者而言，更有价值的跟踪项不是单日涨幅能否再扩大，而是求解器竞争是否更活跃、协议真实交易意图是否增长、代币流通与解锁节奏是否带来供给压力，以及反弹过程中的量价是否匹配。把本轮行情先理解为流动性与动量共振下的快速定价修正，比急于给出单边结论更为审慎。市场波动无法预演，信息完整度也有限，任何解读都应保留修正空间。

US 30-year borrowing costs surge to 5.25%: a global bond-market selloff triggers a domino effect—what exactly are they afraid of?

A global long-bond selloff → borrowing costs spike → liquidity tightens, and BTC gets the first cut.

Last night, the global bond market played out a real “mass escape.” France’s 30-year government bond yield jumped to around 4.85%. The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield then surged straight to 5.25%, hitting a multi-year high, and long bonds in Germany and Japan are being dumped in sync as well.

Pay attention to the logic: when yields rise, bond prices fall. Holders would rather cut losses and run, which suggests the market no longer wants these countries’ long-term IOUs.

In plain terms, it’s one thing: with developed-country fiscal deficits unable to be contained and expectations of repeated inflation, investors demand higher interest to be willing to lend to governments for the long term.
One-sentence translation: it’s not that a single country has a problem—rather, the “sovereign credit” of all developed countries is being repriced collectively, and the global floor price for borrowing has been lifted overall.

Market impact
- Short term: the transmission path is very direct—the 30-year U.S. Treasury yield is the anchor for global asset pricing. When the anchor rises, valuation headroom for risk assets like stocks and crypto gets compressed. When institutions reduce risk, they usually first dump the most liquid assets; BTC is hit first. If ETF flows turn into net outflows, selling pressure will intensify further. Right now BTC is still holding around $63,063 and ETH around $1,884, but honestly this is a lagging reaction; the bond market’s calculation hasn’t really caught up to crypto yet.
- Medium term: if borrowing costs stay elevated for a long time, it effectively lengthens the liquidity-tightening cycle. Rate-cut expectations keep getting pushed back, making it hard for crypto to break out into an independent trend. In addition, as fiscal gaps widen, the probability that regulators will target crypto—this “fat tax” to go after—actually increases.

My take
Short term: clearly bearish. I haven’t seen any “peak yield” signals from the U.S. 30-year yield so far. In this environment, BTC hovering above $63,000 won’t last long. Downside first: watch the $62,000 integer level—if it breaks, expect it to run toward the psychological $60,000 mark. For rebound resistance, check whether $65,000 can be reclaimed. U.S. average car age hits a record high of 12.8 years, yet smart cars may be phased out even earlier than smartphones: why?

American cars are lasting longer on the road, but the software lifespan is getting shorter and shorter—another crack in the tech stock narrative.

CNBC citing the latest data from Mobility Global: the average age of cars on U.S. roads has risen to 12.8 years, a new record high. On the surface, that sounds good, suggesting cars are built to last. But analysts immediately pour cold water: with today’s software-defined vehicles, driven by in-car computers, OTA online upgrades, and constant connectivity, the car is essentially a smartphone with four wheels. Once the hardware becomes outdated and the manufacturer stops supporting it, features “disappear” one by one—driver-assistance functions stop working, the infotainment system lags, and subscription services get shut down. Even Rivian’s chief software officer has been pulled into discussions about this problem. In short: the mechanical lifespan is 12.8 years, but the software lifespan may be much shorter. The auto industry is effectively copying the smartphone playbook of “planned obsolescence.”

Impact on the market
- Short term: The news itself may not be big, but it hits a very tricky nerve. For players in software-defined cars like Tesla and Rivian, valuations hide a key assumption—that once the cars are sold, software revenue can keep rolling in indefinitely. If it becomes consensus that “a car is like a phone—stop updates means stop updates,” institutions will revisit and discount tech companies’ user-lifetime revenue. When tech stocks’ risk appetite gets squeezed, the crypto market—closely tracking the Nasdaq—takes an immediate hit. BTC is currently at $63,040.02, up only 0.51%, showing little momentum. ETH is stuck around $1,883.79; as soon as tech stocks turn red, crypto here will likely fall even faster.
- Medium term: If regulators begin requiring automakers to commit to a software maintenance period, the entire smart-car supply chain—chips, cloud services, and subscription revenues—will have to be re-priced. It may not be bad in the long run, but in the short term, it’s all uncertainty.

My take
I lean cautious and bearish. The correlation between BTC and tech stocks hasn’t fully broken yet. Even if this kind of “tech narrative gets dismantled” news doesn’t trigger an immediate sell-off that same day, it will make institutions pull back the hands that would otherwise be ready to absorb the drop. I couldn’t help but sigh—if even the official team, while testing their own code, has to worry about mixing up models, just how hostile to humans must this Gas-matching mechanism be? Even the creators are afraid someone will mess it up.

There’s no denying that the dual-track design of alternating light and dark—Moonlight handling the public ledger, Phoenix covering privacy needs—is genuinely brilliant. But when it comes to actual development, it’s practically a huge pitfall. Take the moonlight_to_phoenix conversion interface, for example: the documentation plainly says that moonlight_nonce has to be incremented manually by the caller. That kind of logic is suffocating. As long as a real person is typing on a keyboard, mistakes are bound to happen. Miss that line once, and the user’s real money gets frozen halfway.

What’s even more maddening is its fee-charging rules. If you want to operate across models, the fee-paying channel must match the source of funds exactly, with no deviation at all. That forces developers, when writing contracts, to switch environments as carefully as walking on a balance beam. One small mistake, and the whole transaction is ruined.

Thinking back to the PLONK vulnerability uncovered by OtterSec before, the entire privacy-conversion chain was hit hard. A massive flaw that could let someone conjure up $60 million out of thin air somehow slept in the underlying verification layer for two years. If even the core cryptography can pull such a blunder, and now we still expect peripheral developers to manually control nonce values and complex fees, who would dare guarantee absolute safety?

To put it plainly, building such a mechanism with extremely low fault tolerance, without a reliable automated toolkit to help, is basically planting a time bomb for a future systemic collapse.
